A.explanation: This has $\text{m}^{-2}$ left over, which would mean the $\text{m}^2$ from energy was divided twice by area.

B.explanation: This is the base-unit form of energy in joules, $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$, before dividing by area and time.

Divide that energy unit by $\text{m}^2$ for per unit area, then by $\text{s}$ for per unit time, and cancel the powers of $\text{m}$.
walkthrough: Write intensity from the definition as $intensity = energy/(area \times time)$, so unit = $\text{J m}^{-2} \text{s}^{-1}$.
Express the joule in base units: from $W = Fs$, $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{m} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-2}$.
